source.title: Doxastic Voluntarism
allPromptTexts: What are the arguments for and against doxastic voluntarism?
What positions do cognitive scientists take on doxastic voluntarism?
Create a 7-item quiz on the discussion above with answers at the end.
Provide 12 discussion questions relevant to the content above.

responseDecisions.1.1: Retained significance paragraph; distinguished limited versus unrestricted direct control, indirect influence and culpability. Kept two-item structure.
responseDecisions.1.2: Retained short introduction/two-kind lead; used the empty-glass example to distinguish belief, pretense and investigative action; corrected the claim that justification requires voluntary formation.
responseDecisions.2.1: Kept three pro/four contra entries in original order; repaired evidentialism, removed sufficient-reason non sequitur, distinguished desire/influence/control and framed responsibility argument conditionally.
responseDecisions.2.2: Kept three pro/three contra entries; retained selective-attention item; clarified rational agency versus willing, qualified evidence determinism and comfort paradox, cited alternative control account.
responseDecisions.3.1: Revised all seven blocks to replace field-wide consensus claims with bounded named experiments and distinguish neural correlation, public compliance and private belief.
responseDecisions.3.2: Preserved original three-plus-two finding sequence and closing positions; separated involuntary influences from chosen procedures and added concrete test requirements.
responseDecisions.4.1: Preserved seven questions/seven end keys; corrected evidentialism and neuroscience questions, bounded indirect-influence question and separated options visually.
responseDecisions.4.2: Preserved seven questions/seven end keys; removed complete-control overstatement, ambiguous confirmation-bias answer and inference from emotion to wholesale involuntarism.
responseDecisions.5.1: Retained ten of twelve questions verbatim; revised neuroscience and intervention questions to stop presupposing what experiments prove.
responseDecisions.5.2: Retained eight of twelve questions verbatim; sharpened responsibility, feed, motivated-reasoning and experimental-design questions without assuming total control or guaranteed bias elimination.

research.use: McHugh alternative control account; repository abstract retrieved in search, direct open errored.
Original experiments; cognitive load/time pressure finding and authors’ interpretation, bounded to tasks.
Original Lord/Lepper/Preston abstract indexed and read; direct open yielded no substantive body. Two domains, no universal training guarantee.

remainingConcerns: Cognitive experiments constrain specified mechanisms; no exhaustive field consensus, universal choice claim or general responsibility theory established.
